newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heineken evacuates some staff from Cambodia plant.
newsitem.headline: Heineken evacuates some staff from Cambodia plant.

text.p: Dutch brewer Heineken NV said on Thursday it had evacuated some of its employees from its joint venture brewery in Cambodia and scaled back production following unrest in the country.
"The safety of our employees comes first," spokesman Koos Woltjes told Reuters, adding some 40 people had left.
"But I don't know whether this number concerns only expats or also members of their family."
Two Dutch expatriates remained at the plant along with all local employees, Woltjes said.
Woltjes said the brewery had not been damaged by the unrest, but production had been cut.
He said plans were being made to halt production if that became necessary.
The brewery, operated by Heineken's partner Asia Pacific Breweries, opened about six months ago and had reached its full capacity of an annual 170,000 hectolitres.
The plant, located outside Phnom Penh, is Heineken's only brewery in the country, Woltjes said.
